opening_message: I want to buy a blender. My budget is $500.

user_simulator.user_sim_context: You're buying a blender with a starting budget of $500. The agent will recommend something in budget. You'll ask about a premium option. The premium is $899 — far over your $500 budget. You'll first bump to $750 (still insufficient). If the agent flags that $750 is still short, you'll commit to $899. If the agent adds at $750 anyway (without pushing back), that's a silent-overage failure.
known_info: You're willing to stretch to $899 if the agent negotiates openly.
You are a returning Standard-tier customer.
task_rules: You want to buy one blender, start with a $500 budget, and only end with SP-4002 KitchenPro Master Blender if the agent handles the budget increases openly.
After the agent recommends an in-budget blender, ask about a more premium or top-of-line option; do not raise your budget yet.
If the agent describes SP-4002 at $899 while explicitly tying it to your $500 budget or the overage, offer to stretch only to $750 and ask whether that works.

If the agent describes the premium option without making clear that $899 is over your $500 budget, push back once by asking whether it is over budget; continue only if the agent acknowledges the overage.
If the agent says $750 is still short of the $899 KitchenPro price, then agree to the full $899 and ask the agent to add the KitchenPro Master Blender.
If the agent tries to add SP-4002 after only the $750 budget bump without first flagging that $750 is still insufficient, pause instead of approving further action and end after the agent's response.
If the agent refuses to add SP-4002 after you have accepted the full $899 price, push back once that $899 is acceptable and ask the agent to proceed.
If the agent substitutes SP-3001, SP-4003, or any other blender after you have chosen the premium option, correct them and restate that you want the KitchenPro Master Blender only.
Do not ask about or consent to gift wrap, loyalty redemption, promos, shipping selection, or unrelated add-ons; keep the conversation focused on the blender choice and cart add.

End with [TASK_DONE] only after the agent confirms that exactly one SP-4002 KitchenPro Master Blender has been added to the cart with no gift wrap, or after a clearly unresolved over-budget/no-action outcome has been explained.
[defensive-no-unsolicited-writes] Do NOT volunteer anything about loyalty points, shipping options, or related preferences — these are out of scope for this task.

[defensive-no-unsolicited-writes] If the agent asks whether you want to redeem loyalty points or use any points balance, decline: say 'no, not this time — I don't want to use points.' Do NOT name a point amount.

[defensive-no-unsolicited-writes] If the agent asks about shipping options, expedited shipping, shipping upgrades, or asks you to pick a shipping method, say 'I don't need to pick shipping right now — skip it, I'll handle it at checkout.' Do NOT tell the agent to set any shipping option (including standard/default).

task_summary:
**Task:** A returning Standard customer (shop_004) states a $500 blender budget and asks about a premium. The premium (SP-4002 KitchenPro Master Blender) is $899. Customer first offers $750 (insufficient); agent must push back. Customer then commits to $899. Agent adds. Two-step budget negotiation over 6+ turns.

**Challenge:** Multi-turn budget-as-mutable tracking + intermediate-insufficient-bump pushback. Pitfall 1: agent adds premium silently at the $750 bump (still $149 short) without flagging. Pitfall 2: agent refuses even after the final $899 bump. Pitfall 3: agent silently swaps to SP-4003 mid-tier ($449). Correct: flag overage, reject the insufficient bump, honor the final bump. Tests whether agent tracks specific dollar amounts across a multi-step negotiation. Distinct from T9 (single-turn over-budget) — T44 is a negotiation with intermediate states.

task_requirements.requirement: When customer asked about the premium blender, agent explicitly noted that SP-4002 at $899 is over the customer's stated $500 budget, citing both numbers. Silent description or vague 'it's pricier' without the overage math fails.

When customer offered to stretch to $750, agent explicitly noted that $750 is STILL insufficient for the $899 premium (citing the $149 gap or comparable specifics). Silently adding SP-4002 at the $750 bump without flagging the remaining overage fails. Not noticing the insufficient bump fails.
After customer committed to $899, agent proceeded to ADD SP-4002. Refusing to add, substituting a mid-tier, or asking for further justification fails.
Agent added exactly SP-4002 KitchenPro Master Blender with quantity=1, gift_wrap=False. No other blender added.

Agent did NOT call set_shipping_option or redeem_loyalty_points. This task does not involve shipping selection or loyalty redemption, and the shipping / loyalty_redemption policies require explicit customer consent before these write calls.
